news.title: National Gas publishes its 2026 winter outlook
news.summary: National Gas’s outlook assesses supply and demand resilience for winter 2026/27. It says domestic UK Continental Shelf gas production is forecast to decline by around 5% and gas-fired power generation could reach around 27 GW on a peak-demand day. International market disruptions may affect conditions.

news.title: NESO expects electricity supplies to remain secure this winter
news.summary: NESO’s Winter Outlook forecasts a 5.9 GW supply surplus, a 9.5% buffer above peak winter demand, despite international market turbulence.

news.title: Government approves the Jackdaw gas field
news.summary: DESNZ says production could begin from the end of October and peak output could increase domestic gas production by around 6%. Approval does not set wholesale prices or guarantee lower bills.

news.title: Government sets priorities for future water bills and investment
news.summary: The Guardian reports that the Environment Secretary has called for the next price review to prioritise value for money, leak prevention and sewage-spill reduction. This is not a new business water tariff decision.

news.title: Ofwat consults on protections for small-business water customers
news.summary: Ofwat is consulting on protections against detrimental changes to default water retail contracts for smaller business customers in England and Wales. Responses are due 18 November 2026; no tariff decision has been reported.

news.title: Government announces £25m peatland restoration grant scheme
news.summary: The scheme is expected to run from April 2027 to April 2029 and support work intended to help manage flood and drought risks and improve water quality. It does not change business water tariffs.

In the latest published forward curve, Q1 2027 is the most expensive listed power delivery period at £189.90/MWh (18.99p/kWh); Summer 2028 is the cheapest at £86.09/MWh (8.61p/kWh). For gas, November 2026 is the most expensive listed delivery period at 238.36p/therm (8.13p/kWh); Summer 2028 is the cheapest at 106.84p/therm (3.65p/kWh). On 26 October, Q1 2027 power rose 3.22% and November gas rose 3.26% against 23 October. The January household cap forecasts span £1,999.28–£2,185 a year, above the current £1,723 cap. These rising forward prices support early price discovery, but wholesale prices and household caps are not business quotes.

invoice.intro: Business energy bills combine wholesale energy, networks, balancing, policy charges, tax and metering. Fixed contracts may bundle costs into unit and standing charges; flexible contracts may show them separately. Rates are included only where published and checked. Confirm treatment against your contract and site eligibility.

charges.name: Wholesale electricity
charges.whatItIs: The cost of electricity bought by the supplier on wholesale markets.
charges.onYourBill: Usually built into the unit rate; flexible contracts may show the purchasing basis separately.

charges.name: DUoS (distribution use of system)
charges.whatItIs: Regional charges for local distribution networks. Rates depend on location, voltage, time band and site capacity.
charges.onYourBill: May appear as time-band unit, fixed or capacity charges, or be bundled into the contract.

charges.name: TNUoS (transmission network use of system)
charges.whatItIs: Charges for use of the national high-voltage transmission network. A single rate does not apply to every site.
charges.onYourBill: May be passed through as a daily or capacity charge, or included in the contract price.

charges.name: BSUoS (balancing services)
charges.whatItIs: NESO’s charge for balancing the electricity system, recovered through fixed six-month tariffs.
charges.onYourBill: May appear as a per-kWh pass-through charge or be bundled in the unit rate.

charges.name: Renewables Obligation (RO)
charges.whatItIs: Funds eligible renewable generation through supplier certificate obligations or buy-out payments. The 2026/27 calculation uses a £69.34 buy-out price and 0.472 ROCs/MWh.
charges.onYourBill: Usually passed through per kWh or included in the unit rate. Eligible EII certificate holders are exempt.

charges.name: Contracts for Difference (CfD) levy
charges.whatItIs: Funds payments that top up eligible low-carbon generators to their agreed strike prices.
charges.onYourBill: Usually a per-kWh pass-through line, subject to reconciliation. Eligible EII certificate holders are exempt.

charges.name: Nuclear RAB levy (Sizewell C)
charges.whatItIs: Quarterly levy funding Sizewell C under the Regulated Asset Base model.
charges.onYourBill: May appear as a per-kWh pass-through line. Check change-in-law terms on older fixed contracts. Eligible EII certificate holders are exempt.

charges.name: Capacity Market
charges.whatItIs: Pays capacity providers to be available when the system needs electricity. Supplier costs vary with demand and settlement arrangements.
charges.onYourBill: May be passed through per kWh, often with winter peak consumption affecting site charges.

charges.name: Feed-in Tariff (FiT) levy
charges.whatItIs: Supplier-recovered costs associated with the closed small-scale Feed-in Tariff scheme.
charges.onYourBill: May be bundled into the unit rate or shown as a pass-through charge. Eligible EII certificate holders are exempt.

charges.name: EII Support Levy
charges.whatItIs: Funds the network-charge compensation scheme for eligible energy-intensive industries. No single current customer £/MWh rate was verified.
charges.onYourBill: Suppliers may recover their levy costs through customer prices.

charges.name: EII exemption and network-charge compensation
charges.whatItIs: Eligible energy-intensive businesses may apply for exemptions from specified policy costs and compensation for specified network charges, subject to scheme rules.
charges.onYourBill: Give the current certificate to the supplier and check eligible consumption and charges are treated correctly.

charges.name: Climate Change Levy (CCL)
charges.whatItIs: A tax on taxable business energy supplies. Climate Change Agreement participants may qualify for reduced rates.
charges.onYourBill: Normally charged as a separate line before VAT; check site exemptions and any eligible reduced rate.

charges.name: VAT on electricity
charges.rate: 20% standard business rate; 0% for qualifying supplies during the temporary period
charges.period: Temporary 0% from 1 Oct 2026 to 31 Mar 2027 for qualifying supplies
charges.whatItIs: VAT treatment depends on the supply and site eligibility. The temporary zero rate does not apply to every business electricity supply.
charges.onYourBill: Check the VAT rate applied to each site and period of consumption.

charges.name: Metering and settlement charges
charges.whatItIs: May include meter operator, data collection, data aggregation and settlement services.
charges.onYourBill: May be a separate daily or monthly charge, or bundled into the standing charge.

charges.name: Wholesale gas
charges.whatItIs: The cost of gas bought by the supplier, commonly benchmarked to the NBP.
charges.onYourBill: Usually built into the p/kWh unit rate.

charges.name: Gas transportation (NTS and LDZ)
charges.period: Set by applicable tariffs and contract
charges.whatItIs: Charges for the national transmission system and local gas distribution networks, alongside applicable shipper and industry costs.
charges.onYourBill: May be bundled into unit and standing charges or shown separately on larger pass-through contracts.

charges.name: Green Gas Levy
charges.whatItIs: Funds the Green Gas Support Scheme through charges on licensed gas suppliers.
charges.onYourBill: Often recovered through the supplier’s standing or unit charge.

charges.name: Climate Change Levy (CCL)
charges.whatItIs: A tax on taxable business gas supplies. Climate Change Agreement participants may qualify for reduced rates.
charges.onYourBill: Normally charged as a separate line before VAT; check site exemptions and any eligible reduced rate.

charges.name: VAT on gas
charges.rate: 20% standard business rate; 5% on qualifying domestic-rate supplies
charges.whatItIs: VAT treatment depends on the supply and site eligibility. The temporary 0% electricity measure does not apply to gas.
charges.onYourBill: Check the VAT rate applied to the site and period of consumption.

charges.name: Gas metering charges
charges.whatItIs: Charges associated with the gas meter asset and meter services.
charges.onYourBill: May appear as a daily charge or be included in the standing charge.
